questions.:question/problem: Which of the following lines is parallel to $6x - 4y = 9$?
Which of the following lines is parallel to $8x-y=2?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
For two lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of the line $8x-y=2,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}8x-y & =2 \\ -y & =-8x+2 \\ y & =8x-2.\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $8.$

From the given options, the only line that has a slope of $8$ is $y=8x-3.$

questions.:question/problem: Which of the following lines is parallel to $2x+3y=6$?
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Parallel lines have the same slope. First convert the given line to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2x+3y &=6 \\
3y &=-2x+6 \\
y &=-\frac{2}{3}x+2
\end{aligned}
$$

The required slope is $-\frac{2}{3}$. The choices are also in standard form, so isolate $y$ to compare their slopes:

$$
\begin{aligned}
3x+2y=9 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-\frac{3}{2}x+\frac{9}{2} \\
4x+6y=-6 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-\frac{2}{3}x-1 \\
2x-3y=6 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=\frac{2}{3}x-2 \\
2x+6y=6 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-\frac{1}{3}x+1 \\
3x-2y=9 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=\frac{3}{2}x-\frac{9}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Only $4x+6y=-6$ has slope $-\frac{2}{3}$. Its $y$-intercept is $-1$, different from $2$, so it is a distinct parallel line.

Therefore, choose $4x+6y=-6$.

questions.:question/problem: Which of the following is a distinct line parallel to $3x-2y=6$?
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Parallel lines are distinct lines with the same slope. Convert the given line to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
3x-2y &=6 \\
-2y &=-3x+6 \\
y &=\frac{3}{2}x-3
\end{aligned}
$$

Now rewrite each choice:

$$
\begin{aligned}
6x-4y=12 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=\frac{3}{2}x-3 \\
-6x+4y=8 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=\frac{3}{2}x+2 \\
3x+2y=6 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-\frac{3}{2}x+3 \\
2x-3y=6 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=\frac{2}{3}x-2 \\
6x-2y=6 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=3x-3
\end{aligned}
$$

The equations $6x-4y=12$ and $-6x+4y=8$ both have slope $\frac{3}{2}$. But $6x-4y=12$ is just twice the original equation: it describes the same line, with the same $y$-intercept of $-3$. It is not a distinct parallel line.

The equation $-6x+4y=8$ has slope $\frac{3}{2}$ and $y$-intercept $2$. It describes a different line with the same slope. The other three choices have different slopes.

Therefore, choose $-6x+4y=8$.

To find the slope of the line $12x-y=3,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}12x-y & =3 \\ -y & =-12x+3 \\ y & =12x-3.\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $12.$

From the given options, the only line that has a slope of $12$ is $y = 12x+1.$
